messages.content: 你能使用 get_stock_prices 函數來檢索蘋果、微軟、亞馬遜和特斯拉分別在1週、2週、3週和1個月的時間範圍內的股價嗎？。

function.name: get_stock_prices
function.description: Retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

companies.description: List of companies to retrieve stock prices for.

duration.description: Time duration to retrieve stock prices for. E.g., '1 week', '2 weeks', '1 month', etc.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to use get_stock_prices function to retrieve stock prices for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Tesla for durations 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, 1 month. The function signature expects companies: string[], duration: string. But we need to call it multiple times? The user says "retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration". They want separate durations for each company? Actually they say "蘋果、微軟、亞馬遜和特斯拉分別在1週、2週、3週和1個月的時間範圍內的股價". That implies Apple for 1 week, Microsoft for 2 weeks, Amazon for 3 weeks, Tesla for 1 month. So we need to call get_stock_prices four times with single company each and respective duration.

We should produce calls to the function. According to guidelines, we can only call one function at a time. We need to decide which call first. Probably call for Apple first. Then after receiving result, call next. But we can also combine? The function expects array of companies; but we can pass single company. So we can call get_stock_prices with companies: ["Apple"], duration: "1 week". Then next call with ["Microsoft"], "2 weeks", etc.

We need to output function calls. According to guidelines, we should not output anything else. So we will call function for Apple. Then we will wait for response. But we can also chain calls? The guidelines say we can only call one function at a time. So we will call for Apple first. Then after receiving result, we can call next. But we need to produce the function call now. So we will produce the first call. Then we will wait for the function response. Then we will call next. But the user asked to retrieve all four. We can do sequential calls. So we will call for Apple first. Then after we get result, we call for Microsoft, etc.

Thus we produce the first function call.
